note: Synthetic retrieval fixtures. Every sentence below was invented for this test suite and quotes no real source, so the synthetic-fixture policy holds for text as it does for audio. Expected terms are hand-authored rather than generated, because a golden file computed from the implementation asserts nothing.

cases.note: Whitespace-delimited and case-folded; the baseline every other case is compared against.
Non-Latin but whitespace-delimited, so it needs no segmentation.

Right-to-left and whitespace-delimited. This is the case the contract's 'non-Latin/RTL' clause names, and it passes WITHOUT segmentation -- which is why satisfying that clause proves nothing about the scripts that actually fail.
Unsegmented. Without per-character separation the whole run is one term and a two-character query cannot match it.
Kana are not ideographs. A rule written for 'CJK ideographs' leaves this unsegmented, which is how a scope claim covering Japanese came to be shipped against a rule that served only Chinese.

Same class as hiragana, separate block. Deliberately avoids the prolonged sound mark U+30FC, whose tokenizer category is not obvious enough to hand-author an expectation for -- a golden nobody can predict is a golden nobody can check.
Hangul syllables are precomposed and are not ideographs either.
